header.title: Identify Organization State
header.description: This tool helps you perceive whether your experience is isolated or part of a wider culture.

excellent.title: Thriving
excellent.desc: Safe space where mistakes are not feared and diversity is valued.

healthy.title: Healthy
healthy.desc: Basics in order. Occasional conflicts that are solved appropriately.

concern.title: Worrying
concern.desc: Tensions under surface. Cliques, lack of communication, or unclear responsibilities.

warning.title: Toxic
warning.desc: Management by fear, blaming, and constant being on guard.

yellow.title: Yellow Signs
yellow.subtitle: Subtle hints that are easily ignored.
yellow.description: These are 'silent signals'. Often intuition warns about these first.
atmosphere_signs_list: Conversation drying up on difficult topics

check_yourself.label: Check:
check_yourself.text: Do you find yourself explaining others' behavior to yourself? 'He just had a bad day'?

what_to_do.title: What to do?
steps: Ask directly: 'What did you mean by that?'
Do not remain alone with your observation.

orange.title: Orange Signs
orange.subtitle: Clear crossing of boundaries.
orange.description: Situation is no longer normal 'chemistry problem'. Your functioning begins to suffer.

check_yourself.label: Recognize symptoms:
check_yourself.text: Are you starting to doubt your own mental health or professional skills?

what_to_do.title: Act like this:
steps: Contact shop steward or occupational health.

red.title: Red Signs
red.subtitle: Immediate danger to health.
red.description: This is violence. It is no longer about workplace problem, but your safety.
physical_signs_list: Panic attacks when going to work

check_yourself.label: Alarm:
check_yourself.text: If you think 'do I deserve this', you are already deep in trauma. YOU DO NOT DESERVE.

what_to_do.title: Save yourself:
steps: Go to doctor and take sick leave.
File criminal report if threshold is crossed.
Prepare resignation to secure your health.

quicktest.result_desc: You have now identified features of your organization's culture. Remember these are only indicative observations.

scenarios.text: When you suggest a change, it is ignored in meeting, but later someone else presents same idea as their own invention and gets thanks.
scenarios.explanation: This is idea theft and rendering invisible, which is a common form of power use.

scenarios.text: Your supervisor gives you constant tasks that are well below your skill level, without justification.
scenarios.explanation: This can be belittling of work tasks, attempting to erode professional self-esteem.

scenarios.text: Coworker disagrees with decision you made and presents counter-arguments in meeting.
scenarios.explanation: This is normal professional disagreement and conflict that belongs to work.

scenarios.text: In meetings, others constantly interrupt you, but listen carefully when others speak.
scenarios.explanation: Systematic silencing and lack of respect is a form of power abuse.

scenarios.text: Your supervisor gives you direct feedback about your work in private, including negative feedback.
scenarios.explanation: Constructive, private feedback is normal management practice.

scenarios.text: You learn about important meetings only afterwards, even though the topic concerns your work.
scenarios.explanation: Withholding information and excluding you is a classic form of bullying.

scenarios.text: A colleague is often late to meetings, which annoys you.
scenarios.explanation: One person's bad behavior isn't bullying you - it's their problem.

scenarios.text: During lunch break, others go silent when you sit down, and conversations start only after you leave.
scenarios.explanation: Social isolation and making someone invisible is clear bullying.

scenarios.text: Your supervisor asks you to work overtime due to an urgent project.
scenarios.explanation: Occasional overtime requests to handle work tasks are normal, unless it targets only you.

scenarios.text: Coworkers spread rumors about your private life throughout the organization.
scenarios.explanation: Violating privacy and gossiping is manipulation and bullying.

scenarios.text: You receive an email requesting clarification on a work-related matter.
scenarios.explanation: Normal work communication and clarifying questions are not bullying.

scenarios.text: Your supervisor yells at you in front of everyone about a mistake you made.
scenarios.explanation: Public humiliation is always wrong and violates human dignity.

scenarios.text: A team member asks if you could help them with a task where you have more experience.
scenarios.explanation: Asking for help and peer support are signs of a healthy workplace.

scenarios.text: Everyone else on the team gets invited to a social event, but you're not invited.
scenarios.explanation: Deliberate exclusion from social situations is isolation.

scenarios.text: Your supervisor forbids you from talking about the problem to anyone else in the organization.
scenarios.explanation: Culture of silence and silencing enables bullying to continue.

scenarios.text: You have to wait longer for your supervisor's feedback than others on the team.
scenarios.explanation: Supervisor's busyness may explain the delay - you can't conclude bullying from one instance.

scenarios.text: You're given impossible deadlines for tasks on purpose, so that you fail.
scenarios.explanation: Deliberately causing failure is power abuse and sabotage.

scenarios.text: A coworker laughs out loud when you make a mistake in a presentation.
scenarios.explanation: Humiliating and mocking someone for a momentary lapse in professional competence is offensive.

scenarios.text: In a project group, different members have different views on how to proceed.
scenarios.explanation: Different opinions and perspectives are normal teamwork and conflict.

scenarios.text: Your supervisor continuously gives you tasks that are clearly below your professional level.
scenarios.explanation: Deliberately forcing underperformance and limiting competence is bullying.

team_checklist.title: Team Checklist
team_checklist.subtitle: Go through your team's basic functions.

status.crisis_text: Team is in critical state. Immediate intervention needed.
status.healthy_text: Team's basic functions seem to be in order.

interaction.title: Interaction and Communication
interaction.description: How do you encounter one another?
items: Feedback is given constructively and privately
Criticism is balanced - everyone receives it
Praise is given publicly, reprimands privately
Mistakes are treated as learning opportunities
Jokes do not target one person
Inappropriate behavior is addressed when pointed out

information.title: Information Flow and Decision Making
items: Everyone receives the same information at the same time
Meeting invitations are sent to everyone relevant
Decisions are justified transparently
Changes are announced in advance
Resources are distributed equitably
Expectations are clear and consistent

power_dynamics.title: Power Dynamics and Hierarchy
items: The supervisor listens and accepts feedback
Hierarchy does not prevent open discussion
Mistakes can be discussed without fear
Disagreements are resolved professionally
Everyone has an equal right to be heard
Authority is not misused

atmosphere.title: Atmosphere and Community
items: People chat casually with each other
No one is systematically left out
Lunches and breaks are spent together
Successes are celebrated as a team
Help is asked for and given freely
The atmosphere doesn't change when someone enters

emotional.title: My Emotional Reactions
items: You enjoy your work most of the time
You sleep well, don't wake up thinking about work
Going to work does not cause anxiety
You can be yourself at work
You trust your colleagues and supervisor
You feel you belong to the community

self_assessment.title: Self-Assessment
self_assessment.description: Assess your own coping and experience in current situation.

culture.title: Organizational Culture
culture.desc: What is your workplace atmosphere like?

situations.high_risk_desc: Your symptoms suggest severe stress state.
situations.low_risk_desc: Your symptoms are under control, but monitor situation.

cultures.excellent_desc: Things seem to be well in organization.
cultures.bad_desc: There are serious problems in work community.

itsetunto.text: Do you doubt your abilities to perform tasks that felt easy before?
Do you feel like an outsider in your work community?
Is your work criticized constantly without clear reason?
Have you been yelled or cursed at?
Has your self-esteem dropped in your current job?

todellisuus.text: Do you feel your words are twisted or intentionally misunderstood?
Do you blame yourself for what happened?
Does it feel like you are being watched or monitored?
Do you feel guilty about situation you can't control?
Are you ashamed to tell loved ones about situation?

eristyksissä.text: Are you left uninvited to meetings or lunches?
Does your supervisor or colleague avoid eye contact with you?
Is there gossip about you behind your back?
Have you been forbidden from talking to others?
Do you feel you cannot trust anyone at work?

fyysiset.text: Do you have trouble sleeping because of work matters?
Do you feel anxiety on Sunday evenings or during commute?
Do you have physical symptoms (headache, stomach pain) on workdays?
Do you feel 'on guard' all the time at work?
Does your heart pound when you think about work?

käyttäytyminen.text: Is your workload unreasonable compared to others?
Have work tasks been taken away from you without justification?
Are false rumors being spread about you?
Has your opinion been ignored repeatedly?
Have you considered resigning because of the situation?

leadership.text: My supervisor belittles subordinates' worries or ideas.
Withholding information is common as tool of power.
It is safe to disagree with leader in meetings.
I dare to tell about my mistakes without fear of punishment or embarrassment.
If I notice a grievance, I can raise it safely.

community.text: People gossip behind others' backs in my team.
We have inner circles that are hard to get into.
Colleagues defend each other if someone behaves inappropriately.
We value diversity and it is not a subject of jokes.
I feel I have to watch my words constantly.

interaction.text: Everyone receives the same information at the same time
Meeting invitations are sent to everyone relevant
Jokes are not repeatedly targeted at one person
Lunch and breaks are spent together
No one is systematically left out
Atmosphere problems can be discussed openly
If I point out offensive behavior, it is reacted to
Teasing is not excused as "just a joke"

support.text: I know where to report bullying concerns
Contact info for occupational safety rep is easily available
Processes for bullying cases are clear
I can raise concerns without fear of consequences
Those who intervene are supported, not punished

psych_safety.text: I can be myself at work
Mistakes can be discussed without fear
Help is asked for and given freely
I feel I belong to the community
The atmosphere does not change when someone enters

courage.text: I would intervene if I observed inappropriate behavior
I would intervene even if the target was an influential person
My colleagues would support me if I intervened
I know a safe way to intervene
I have intervened in the last 3 months after observing misconduct

monitoring.text: Survey results lead to concrete actions
Training on identifying bullying is organized

risk.medium: Your symptoms are worrying. Pay attention to recovery.
risk.high: You likely need professional help for coping.

culture.medium: Culture has challenges that should be addressed.

culture.low: Leadership is inconsistent or authoritarian. Trust in supervisors is weak.
culture.medium: Leadership works partially, but transparency and fairness need improvement.
culture.high: Leadership is exemplary, fair, and inclusive. Trust is solid.

culture.low: There are cliques and exclusion in the community. The atmosphere is unsafe.
culture.medium: The community functions routinely, but deeper belonging or support may be missing.
culture.high: The community is tight-knit, supportive, and values diversity.

culture.low: The atmosphere is alarming. Bullying or discrimination occurs and is not addressed.
culture.medium: There are tensions in the atmosphere. Information flow is broken or groups are cliquey.
culture.high: Interaction is open and inclusive. People feel comfortable and that they belong.

culture.low: Processes are missing or non-functional. Seeking help is felt to be difficult.
culture.medium: Structures exist, but there is ambiguity or slowness in practice.
culture.high: The support network is strong. Processes are clear, fast, and fair.

culture.low: The sense of safety is shattered. Mistakes are hidden and fear prevails.
culture.medium: Safety varies. In some situations openness is possible, in others people are guarded.
culture.high: High psychological safety. People create a safe space for vulnerability and learning.

culture.low: The threshold to intervene is too high. The bystander role is common.
culture.medium: There is a desire to intervene, but means or courage are not always enough.
culture.high: Misconduct is actively addressed. 'We do not look away' is reality.

culture.low: Problems are not monitored or are swept under the rug. Surveys do not lead to action.
culture.medium: Monitoring is occasional or mechanical. Actions often remain incomplete.
culture.high: Development is continuous and data-driven. Problems are reacted to systematically.

risk.medium: You are starting to doubt your perceptions.
risk.high: Your confidence in your own reality is tested.
You feel strongly isolated from the community.
Your body is in high alert. Pause and listen.

risk.medium: You are guarded in social situations.
risk.high: You are altering your behavior to cope.
